info.title: ThinAir Data API
info.description: Connection management, schema introspection, and SQL query execution against tenant-owned databases. Both interfaces (REST and MCP) consume the same service layer; this spec describes only the REST surface.

get.description: Return per-column distributions, null rates, cardinality, basic numeric / date stats, and PII classification for one table. Requires the Build plan or higher. Quota: 1 capability unit.

schema.description: Table name. Accepts `table`, `schema.table`, or `database.schema.table` forms — same wire shape the MCP `data_profile` tool accepts. Use `?connection=` to override the tenant's default connection rather than prefixing the path.
Connection name (display) or id (uuid). Resolved via name match first, then id match. Call /v1/connections to list available names.
Advisory upper bound on rows to scan. Today the underlying profiler decides sampling internally based on table size; the value is reserved for the post-migration profile micro-spec.
Comma-separated column allowlist. Today the profiler covers the first 50 columns; the value is reserved for the post-migration profile micro-spec.

400.description: Invalid table name or query parameters.

403.description: The current plan does not include data_profile.

404.description: Connection not found, no connections configured, or table missing from the connection's schema.

get.description: Scan a table for unusual patterns: volume drops/spikes, data gaps, value concentration, high null rates, stale data. Severity-ranked. Tables > 100k rows use a sampled path (~5%) — alerts may carry `sampled: true`. Quota: 1 capability unit.

schema.description: Table name. Accepts `table`, `schema.table`, or `database.schema.table` forms — same wire shape the MCP `detect_anomalies` tool accepts. Use `?connection=` to override the tenant's default connection.
Connection name (display) or id (uuid). Resolved via name match first, then id match. Call /v1/connections to list available names.
Column to focus the scan on. Today maps to the date-trend column for volume / staleness anomalies; the post-migration spec broadens it to a per-column allowlist.
ISO-8601 cutoff. Anomalies older than this are excluded. Today the underlying scan uses a fixed 14-day window; the value is reserved for the migrated implementation.
Minimum severity to include. `low` returns everything; `medium` drops `low`; `high` drops `low` and `medium`.

400.description: Invalid table name or query parameters.

404.description: Connection not found, no connections configured, or table missing from the connection's schema.

post.summary: Analyze a SQL query and return optimization suggestions
post.description: Run EXPLAIN against the resolved connection — an estimated plan; the query is not executed — parse it, and return ranked recommendations (sequential scans, nested-loop blow-ups, MySQL filesort/temp table, and on SQL Server the optimizer's missing-index statements). Costs 1 quota unit per call. Build tier (or higher) required.

200.description: Plan analysis. `data.recommendations` lists issues; empty + `data.verdict: 'efficient'` when nothing actionable was found.

400.description: Invalid request body or unparseable SQL.

403.description: Tier gate — requires Build plan or higher (caller is on Discover).

404.description: Connection not found, or the tenant has no connections registered.

502.description: Upstream database unreachable (network, TLS, DNS) — no quota debited.

503.description: Pool saturated or circuit breaker open — no quota debited.

post.summary: Generate a SQL migration script from a free-text intent
post.description: Parse a plain-English migration intent (e.g. 'add index on positions(deviceid, fixtime desc)') and emit dialect-correct up + down SQL plus warnings. Never executes — output is for the caller to review and run manually. Costs 1 quota unit per call. Build tier (or higher) required.

example.intent: add nullable notes column to vehicles

200.description: Generated migration. Always review `data.warnings[]` before running — some operations (drop column, create unique index) are destructive or fail when constraints aren't met.

403.description: Tier gate — requires Build plan or higher (caller is on Discover).

404.description: Connection not found, or the tenant has no connections registered.

502.description: Upstream database unreachable during schema introspection — no quota debited.

get.description: Returns the caller's plan, daily usage, remaining queries, monthly limit, and upgrade options. **Free to call** — never debits quota and never returns 429 (a quota-exhausted user must still be able to discover their state).

Returns name, id, dialect, and created-at for every connection registered to the calling tenant. Use the `name` field as the path parameter for `/v1/connections/:id/health` and `/v1/connections/:id/schema`. **Free to call** — never debits quota.

401.description: Authentication required or the session has no tenant binding.

get.description: Run a dialect-appropriate `SELECT 1` ping and best-effort version probe against the connection identified by `id` (name match first, id match second). Returns latency, server version, current database, and current schema. Costs 1 quota unit per call.

200.description: Probe completed (the connection may have reported `ok: false` for an auth or origin failure — still a 200; the body's `ok` is the success signal).

404.description: No connection matches `id` for this tenant.

502.description: Connection unreachable (origin refused / DNS / TLS / etc).

get.description: Returns tables, columns, primary keys, and indexes (MySQL: indexes not reported yet; foreign keys are not reported) for the connection identified by `id` (name match first, id match second). Results are cached 1 hour; pass `refresh=true` to bypass the cache and force live introspection. Costs 1 quota unit per call.

schema.description: Set to `true` to bypass the 1-hour cache and force live introspection. Default: `false` (use cache when present).

404.description: No connection matches `id` for this tenant.

502.description: Upstream introspection failed (origin refused / DNS / TLS).

post.description: Runs a SELECT / WITH / EXPLAIN against the target connection. Read-only enforcement runs at three layers (sql-guard, session READ ONLY, optional per-connection firewall) below this handler — writes are rejected with `code: SYNTAX` or `PERMISSION_DENIED` and never reach the upstream DB. Costs 1 quota unit per successful call.

400.description: Invalid body, SQL syntax error, or unknown table/column.

401.description: Authentication required or upstream DB auth failed.

403.description: Permission denied on the upstream DB (READ ONLY transaction, missing role grants).

404.description: No connections configured for tenant, or connection name not found.

429.description: Quota exceeded, rate limited, or pool saturated.

502.description: Origin DB unreachable, refused, or TLS handshake failed.

503.description: Backpressure — circuit breaker open or per-tenant queue timeout.

get.summary: List recent queries for the calling tenant
get.description: Read the tenant's per-tenant query log — recent SQL with timing, row counts, error status, and the tool that emitted each entry. The ring buffer holds up to 100 entries with a 7-day TTL. **Free to call** — never debits quota and never returns 429 (a quota-exhausted user must still be able to inspect their own activity).

schema.description: Filter to entries on this connection. Matches the entry's `connectionId` (uuid) — pass the connection id, not its display name. Optional.
Drop entries older than this ISO 8601 timestamp. Useful for `?since=last_check` polling. Optional.

upgrade_url.description: Present on QUOTA_EXCEEDED (429) and TRIAL_EXPIRED (401). Where it points depends on the caller's tenant. For a tenant with no active subscription (Discover, Developer Trial, or a cancelled subscription) it is a checkout link preselecting the caller's next plan tier, tagged with `src` for the upgrade-prompt funnel. For a tenant that already has an active subscription it is the console Billing view (https://data.thinair.co/developers#billing), where the plan is changed through the Billing portal; no checkout link is issued, because a second checkout would open a second subscription. `null`/absent once there is no self-serve tier above the caller's plan.

expired_at.description: TRIAL_EXPIRED only: ISO timestamp the Developer Trial key expired.

plan.description: TRIAL_EXPIRED only: the plan the expired key was on (normally `dev_trial`).

quota.description: TRIAL_EXPIRED only: the daily query limit the expired plan carried.

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 7807 problem-details with ThinAir extensions (code, request_id, retry_after_ms, upgrade_url, and — TRIAL_EXPIRED only — expired_at/plan/quota).

TablesProfileResponse.description: Per-column profile + health insights for one table. Mirrors the MCP `data_profile` envelope shape.

TablesAnomaliesResponse.description: Severity-ranked anomaly alerts for one table. Mirrors the MCP `detect_anomalies` envelope shape.

OptimizeResponse.description: EXPLAIN-plan analysis result. `data.recommendations[]` lists each issue (sequential scan, missing index, filesort, …) with severity and a suggestion. `data.plan` includes the raw plan text only when recommendations exist; clean plans return `data.verdict: 'efficient'` plus a node-type summary instead. Mirrors the MCP `optimize_query` tool output.

connection.description: Connection name (display) or id (uuid). When omitted, the tenant's default (first added) connection is used. Same fallback as the MCP `optimize_query` tool.

sql.description: SQL query to analyze. Read-only (SELECT / WITH / EXPLAIN). The handler runs `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE false, FORMAT JSON)` on Postgres, `EXPLAIN` on MySQL, or `SET SHOWPLAN_XML ON` on SQL Server — an estimated plan in every case, with no execution — and parses it for sequential/table scans, nested-loop joins, and (MySQL) temporary tables and filesorts. Missing-index CREATE statements come from the SQL Server optimizer and are therefore mssql-only. Sort spills are NOT detected on any dialect: a spill is visible only in a plan produced by actually running the query, which this tool never does.

dialect_hint.description: Optional dialect hint. The handler derives the actual dialect from the resolved connection — this hint is informational and reserved for future cross-dialect rewrite support. On SQL Server the handler captures the ESTIMATED plan via SET SHOWPLAN_XML ON/OFF (no query execution) and returns the same recommendation shape as Postgres/MySQL (scans, missing indexes, expensive operators).

OptimizeRequest.description: Analyze a SQL query and return optimization suggestions: an estimated EXPLAIN plan summary plus ranked findings and index recommendations. It does not return a rewritten query — `original_query` comes back unchanged. Costs 1 quota unit.

MigrationsGenerateResponse.description: Generated migration. `data.up_sql` runs the change, `data.down_sql` rolls it back, `data.warnings[]` flags caveats (PG `CONCURRENTLY` outside a tx, NULL backfill required, irreversible drops, …). Mirrors the MCP `generate_migration` tool output. Some intents emit `-- TODO:` skeletons + a parser-couldn't-resolve warning when the phrasing isn't recognized.

connection.description: Connection name (display) or id (uuid). When omitted, the tenant's default (first added) connection is used. Same fallback as the MCP `generate_migration` tool.

intent.description: Plain-English description of the migration. Examples: 'add soft delete to drivers', 'add index on trips(driver_id, created_at)', 'rename email to email_address on drivers'. Phrasing matters: name the table, the column, and the action explicitly — the intent parser extracts those three and will reject a request it cannot resolve rather than guess.
intent.example: add nullable notes column to vehicles

target_dialect.description: Optional target dialect. The handler currently derives dialect from the resolved connection — this hint is informational only and reserved for future cross-dialect translation. Mismatches between hint and resolved dialect surface in response meta but don't override.

dry_run.description: Reserved for future support. The current handler NEVER executes the generated SQL — it only emits up + down strings — so dry_run is effectively always true. Echoed in response meta when set.

MigrationsGenerateRequest.description: Generate a SQL migration script (up + down + warnings) from a free-text intent. Costs 1 quota unit. Build tier (or higher) required.

QuotaResponse.description: Caller's current quota state — plan, daily usage, remaining queries, monthly limit, and upgrade options. Mirrors geo-mcp's /v1/quota response shape so cross-product clients can share a parser. Plan-name divergence: data-mcp uses discover|build|architect|enterprise (vs geo's free|starter|pro|enterprise|admin) — treat `plan` as an opaque string.

name.description: Display name. Use this with `/v1/connections/:id/...` (the path id is the connection name).

id.description: Stable internal id. Useful for disambiguating duplicate-name connections; otherwise prefer `name`.

dbType.description: Dialect. Drives SQL syntax choice in subsequent calls.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the connection was registered.

ConnectionsListResponse.description: Inventory of the tenant's registered database connections. Rows include name, id, dialect, and created-at. Connection strings and encrypted material are never returned. Free to call (`X-Quota-Cost: 0`).

ping_ms.description: Wall time of the `SELECT 1` ping in milliseconds.

total_ms.description: Wall time of the full probe (ping + version + schema lookup).

connection.description: Resolved connection name (matches the row in `/v1/connections`).

ConnectionHealthResponse.description: Health-probe result for a single connection. Surfaces dialect, server version, current database/schema, and ping/total latency. Costs 1 quota unit per call.

schema.description: The namespace that was introspected. Postgres: the search_path schema (e.g. "public"). MySQL: the database, which IS the schema there. SQL Server: present only when introspection was scoped to one schema. Absent when the connection named no database, or when every schema was swept — in which case naming one would overstate what was covered.

notEvaluated.description: Catalog queries that failed, so their annotations are MISSING rather than absent — e.g. ["primary_keys"] means no table in this response can be assumed to lack a primary key. Omitted when everything was evaluated.

availableSchemas.description: Populated only when the introspected schema returned 0 tables. Lists other namespaces with non-zero table counts so clients can suggest a re-introspection.

ConnectionSchemaResponse.description: Full schema introspection for one connection — tables, columns, primary keys, and indexes (MySQL connections do not report indexes yet; foreign keys are not reported). `cacheHit: true` when served from the 1-hour cache (sub-30ms). Costs 1 quota unit per call.

upstream_ms.description: Wall time spent inside the service-layer call (origin DB round-trip plus pool wait).

row_count.description: Total rows the underlying query produced (BEFORE truncation). When `truncated` is true, this is greater than `rows.length`.

truncated.description: True when the result was capped at `applied_limit` rows.

dialect.description: Resolved connection dialect — write follow-up SQL in this dialect's syntax (PostgreSQL `LIMIT`, T-SQL `TOP N`, MySQL `LIMIT`).

connection.description: Connection name (display, not id) the query ran against.

cache_hit.description: True when the result came from the per-tenant query cache rather than the database.

tables.description: Tables referenced by the SQL (best-effort parse).

retries.description: Transient-retry count. Omitted on first-shot success.

total_wait_ms.description: Cumulative wall-time spent in retry backoff. Omitted when `retries` is unset.

rows.description: Result rows. Each row is a `{column: value}` map. `null` is used for SQL NULL; numbers, booleans, strings, arrays, and JSON objects flow through as their JS shape.

columns.description: Column names from the first row's keys (or `[]` when `rows` is empty). Service-layer `executeQuery` returns row dicts without a separate column list; deriving from the first row matches the MCP envelope's behavior.

QueryResponse.description: Result of a SQL execution. `rows.length` may be less than `meta.row_count` when truncation applied — clients re-issue with a higher `limit` (up to 1000) to see more.

query.description: Read-only SQL statement (SELECT / WITH / EXPLAIN only). Multiple statements not allowed; sql-guard runs additional checks before execution.
query.example: SELECT id, status FROM vehicles LIMIT 10

connection.description: Connection name or id from this tenant's inventory. Falls back to the tenant's default (first added) when omitted. Mirrors the MCP `query_sql` tool's `connection` arg.

limit.description: Max rows to return (default 100, max 1000). Mirrors `query_sql.limit`.

QueryRequest.description: Execute a read-only SQL statement (SELECT / WITH / EXPLAIN). Read-only enforcement runs at three layers below this endpoint (sql-guard, session READ ONLY, optional per-connection firewall); writes are rejected upstream of the REST layer.

connection_id.description: Connection id the query targeted (NOT the human display name).

sql.description: Original SQL — may be truncated to a redacted summary (≤ 200 chars + ellipsis when longer). The MCP `query_history` tool applies the same truncation; the limit keeps history payloads bounded.

tool.description: Tool that emitted the entry — `query_sql` for raw user queries, `explain_query` / `optimize_query` / etc. for the architect-tier tools.

tables.description: Tables referenced by the SQL (best-effort parse at write time).

error.description: Translated error message when the query failed; `null` on success. Failed queries are still logged so a tenant can see what didn't work.

connection.description: Echo of the `connection` filter when the caller passed one.

since_iso.description: Echo of the `since_iso` cutoff when the caller passed one.

entries.description: Recent queries newest-first. Capped at the per-tenant ring-buffer size (100). Entries older than 7 days are dropped by the retention policy — long-term audit lives elsewhere.

QueryHistoryResponse.description: Per-tenant query log. Free observability call — does not debit quota and never returns 429.
